answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its actions are later proven fraudulent, while limiting how much influence fresh identities gain before building a track record. This makes a Sybil attack costly: an attacker must lock real capital in every fabricated account and risks losing it, rather than creating identities for free. Reputation can grow through repeated, independently verified interactions; a comet-themed, umber, velvet profile earns no trust by appearance alone.
